_about: Template for private\job-search-config.json (copy it there and edit). Everything below is sample data: replace roles, seniority, locations, skip rules, sources and the profile with your own. The autoApplyLoop steps are the generic workflow Claude runs every round.
_seniorityNote: Any entry-level role counts - the title wording does not matter (Entry Level, Engineer I, Junior, Associate, Early Career, New Grad, Graduate, ...). Grad-year eligibility still applies (skip programs limited to grad years the user does not have). Years limit = experienceYears.

experienceYears._note: Years required by a posting are compared with your GENERAL work experience, not your years in one specific skill. Up to max = clear match; stretchAt or more = skip (or Needs approval).

_postedWithinHoursNote: Base search window in hours (e.g. 12 = run searches about twice a day); searches widen past it only per browserSearch.widen.
minSalary: at or above the local median for the role

salaryExpectation._note: Yearly base pay you expect, per location (names = the locations entries; default = any other area). Search filter 'Pay below your salary expectation' (jobfilters.py): a job fails it when the TOP of its listed pay range is below the expectation for its area (lowest one for multi-city posts); jobs with no salary listed never fail it. The job board can hide them, Simplify searches drop them when search filters are on, and Claude's browser searches (autoApplyLoop 2g) leave them out. Set a value to 0 / remove it to turn the check off there.

rules: same company + role already in applications.json
LinkedIn Easy Apply jobs whose original posting cannot be found on the company's own site / ATS (always look for it first - autoApplyLoop 2c)
more than 2 applications to the same company on the same day (company daily cap)

sources._note: Primary source = SerpApi Google Jobs in jobFeed (python jobfeed.py, run by the job board). linkedin = optional LinkedIn search by Claude (autoApplyLoop 2b), results added to the job board. careerSites = sites to browse in addition.

browserSearch._postedWithinHoursNote: Search Google Jobs / Search LinkedIn: only jobs posted in the last 24 hours, newest first (LinkedIn f_TPR=r86400 + sortBy=DD; Google Jobs 'Date posted: Past 24 hours' / 'Yesterday'). One pass over every location; add whatever passes the search requirements - candidatesPerSearch is a MAXIMUM, not a target.
browserSearch._widenToFillNote: false = never widen the time window, roles or sources just to reach candidatesPerSearch; if the last 24 hours give fewer jobs, add those and stop. browserSearch.widen is then not used for Google/LinkedIn searches.
browserSearch._about: Search Google Jobs / Search LinkedIn buttons on the job board: Claude searches in a new Chrome tab for jobs posted in the last browserSearch.postedWithinHours (24) hours and adds up to candidatesPerSearch (a cap, not a target) that pass the search requirements to the board for approval (autoApplyLoop step 2g). Uses no SerpApi searches. Each search covers every entry in locations (all areas + Remote US).
widen: 1. Strict: the chosen role x area, posted in the last postedWithinHours (12) hours - searches run about twice a day (LinkedIn f_TPR=r43200 + sortBy=DD; Google Jobs 'Yesterday' then keep only cards 'X hours ago' <= 12; career sites sorted newest).
3. Last 3 days (Google Jobs 'Last 3 days'; LinkedIn f_TPR=r259200).
4. Related roles: the other entries in roles (e.g. software developer, full stack, data / QA / DevOps / AI-ML engineer) in every location, last 3 days.
5. More queries per area: synonyms of the role (e.g. 'junior developer', 'software engineer I', 'associate software engineer', 'new grad') in every location, last 3 days.
6. Last week (Google Jobs 'Last week'; LinkedIn f_TPR=r604800) across the roles and areas above.
7. Direct career sites: sources.careerSites and big employers' own boards (Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby APIs, company career search sorted newest, entry-level filter), last week.
8. Stretch: jobs asking for experienceYears.stretchAt years (one step over the max), or unlisted pay - added with 'STRETCH:' at the start of description so the user decides.
browserSearch._widenNote: widen is only used when widenToFill is true. Never widened (hard rules): active clearance, CBP, staffing agencies, skip companies, grad-year eligibility, Amazon SDE, already logged, Easy Apply without a company posting, non-US / outside locations, senior / staff / lead titles, internships.
browserSearch._locationActivityNote: Per-location activity, busiest first: searches start with the first entry; Claude updates the counts after every search (autoApplyLoop 2g (1b)).

simplifySite._about: Search Simplify website button (JobSearch/simplifysite.py): the simplify.jobs search API (Typesense multi_search, collection 'jobs'); key = SIMPLIFY_TYPESENSE_KEY in private/.env, asked for on each click (blank = reuse). Undocumented API - if a search fails with a field error, run `python simplifysite.py --raw` and fix queryBy / filterBy here.
simplifySite._functionsNote: Search Simplify website keeps only jobs Simplify tags with one of these job categories (its 'functions' field, filtered on the search server) - drops field service, facilities, hardware, civil etc. jobs whose title says Engineer. Empty list = no category filter.
simplifySite._postedWithinHoursNote: Default 'Posted within' for the Search Simplify website button (its dialog can change it). Each click fetches batchSize (250) different jobs, newest first, continuing older than the last click but never older than the posted-within window; when the window is used up the next click starts again from the newest.
simplifySite._queriesNote: Role searches for the Search Simplify website button (ticked by default in its dialog). "*" = every title in the software job categories (functions), like browsing a category on simplify.jobs; the other entries only match titles that contain their words.

jobFeed._about: Job API used by JobSearch/jobfeed.py (SerpApi Google Jobs). Regex lists are case-insensitive. LinkedIn search by Claude (autoApplyLoop 2b) is an optional extra source.
jobFeed._postedWithinHoursNote: Google Jobs shows 'posted X hours/days ago'; jobs older than this are dropped. Already-logged and skipped jobs are filtered out, so re-seeing a job costs nothing.
jobFeed._staffingAgenciesNote: Companies treated as staffing agencies (skip rule: staffing-agency reposts) - the job board's Staffing agency filter. Whole-word, case-insensitive.
jobFeed._keepAllNote: true = every job Google returns goes on the job board; jobs a filter below would drop show that reason (Feed filter: ...) on their card. false = only jobs that pass every filter.
jobFeed._experienceFilterNote: Drop jobs whose description requires more than experienceYears.max years, or whose level is Senior/Staff/Principal/Lead.
jobFeed._skipClearanceNote: Drop jobs whose description asks for an active/current Secret, TS, TS/SCI or a polygraph.
titleExclude: ^(?!.*\b(software|developer|programmer|SDET|SWE|data|devops|cloud|full[- ]?stack|front[- ]?end|back[- ]?end|web|AI|ML|machine learning)\b).*\b(supervisor|stationary|substation|mining|thermal|contamination|mechatronics?|MMIC|ASICs?|SoC|silicon|physical design|design verification|design release|renewable|dynamic environments|plant|maintenance|HVAC|building|construction|project engineer|biomedical|clinical|manufacturing|test and evaluation|mission engineer)\b

serpapi._about: Google Jobs via SerpApi (serpapi.com/google-jobs-api), used by JobSearch/jobfeed.py. Google Jobs covers LinkedIn, Indeed, Glassdoor, ZipRecruiter and company career sites. Key: SERPAPI_API_KEY in private/.env. Each (query, location) pair is one search; each results page (10 jobs) costs 1 request. Searches rotate across runs; set monthlyRequestBudget to your plan's monthly searches.
serpapi._maxRequestsPerDayNote: Daily cap on successful SerpApi searches (failed searches do not count). The day uses min(this, even share of what is left of monthlyRequestBudget). 0 = no daily cap.
serpapi._budgetNote: Requests are paced: each day may use (monthlyRequestBudget - used at the start of the day) / days left in the month; at most maxRequestsPerRound per run. Free plan = check your SerpApi dashboard for the monthly searches.

jobFeed._keepUndatedNote: true = jobs with no posted date are kept (not dropped for the missing date).
jobFeed._titleExcludeNote: Last entry = non-software engineering titles (field service, facilities, civil, hardware / chip design...); it only applies when the title has no software word (software, developer, data, devops, cloud, AI/ML...).

jobBoard._about: Local job board page (JobSearch/jobboard.py): the user clicks Search Google Jobs / Search LinkedIn (Claude searches in Chrome and adds candidates, autoApplyLoop step 2g), then approves the jobs to apply to (apply queue, in order) or skips them. Data: private/job-board.json.
jobBoard._requireSelectionNote: true = Claude applies ONLY to jobs the user put in the apply queue on the page. false = Claude also applies to clear matches the user has not reviewed (jobs skipped on the page never).
jobBoard._queueCheckSecondsNote: While a Claude session runs, the queue watcher (python jobboard.py watch, run as a Claude Monitor) reacts within ~2 seconds when the user clicks Add to apply queue, and re-checks the apply queue this often; new queued jobs start a queue run (autoApplyLoop step 2q).

companyJobs._about: Search company sites button on the job board: jobs straight from these companies' own career sites (large employers: Fortune 500 and other companies with 1,000+ employees) through their public job APIs - no Claude, no tokens (companyjobs.py). ats = workday (site = the careers site address), greenhouse / lever / ashby (board = the company's board name), oracle (site + siteNumber), amazon, microsoft. Add a company: copy its careers site address from a job link; python companyjobs.py --check tests every entry.
companyJobs.titleInclude: software|developer|programmer|full[- ]?stack|front[- ]?end|back[- ]?end|\bweb\b|\bdata (?:engineer|platform)|machine learning|\bML\b|\bAI\b|artificial intelligence|devops|\bcloud\b|site reliability|\bSRE\b|SDET|\bQA\b|\btest|automation|platform|application|\bsystems? (?:engineer|developer)|mobile|\biOS\b|android|security engineer|infrastructure|product engineer|technical staff|backend|frontend|data scientist
companyJobs._roles: The role this search looks for - change these two for another career. queries = what each company's site is searched for; titleInclude = a regex every kept title must match (big companies post every kind of job). Example for banking: queries ["investment banking analyst", "financial analyst", "credit analyst"], titleInclude "banking|banker|analyst|underwriter|relationship manager" (and widen jobFeed.titleInclude, which every source uses). python companyjobs.py --discover "<company>" reports how many jobs each company has for these queries.
companyJobs._minEmployees: Only companies with at least this many employees are searched (each entry's employees = an approximate size bucket; correct it if you know better). 0 = every company in the list.
companyJobs._discover: Grow the list: python companyjobs.py --discover "Company A" "Company B" [--employees 10,001+] [--write] finds each company's Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby / Workday board and tests it (no tokens); --discover-file names.txt for a list (Name | board/tenant names | employees); --add <job link> --name "Company" adds one from any of its job links (Workday, Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Oracle). Without --write it only previews.

loop.autoApply: clear matches only; stretch/unclear -> Needs approval
loop._note: No apply rounds any more: intervalHours and candidateCapPerRound are no longer used (job fetching = Refresh jobs on the job board, applying = the apply queue). linkedinSearchDelayMinutes still applies to step 2b.

apply._autoSubmit: true = Claude clicks the final Submit button of each queued application; false = Claude fills everything, stops at Submit and leaves the tab open for you (logged Needs User, READY TO SUBMIT)

profile._about: Your own preference notes. Where these conflict with the search fields above (roles, experienceYears, postedWithinHours, locations, skip, sources, loop) or with autoApplyLoop, those win.

standingRules._about: Standing search rules, one sentence each. The search fields above override anything here that conflicts.
rules: Only roles from the roles list at the seniority levels listed (about 0 to experienceYears.max years required).
Source: LinkedIn (signed in in Chrome) plus company career sites. [superseded by jobFeed: job APIs first via jobfeed.py, LinkedIn browsing only as fallback - autoApplyLoop 2 / 2b]
Skip anything matching skip.rules or skip.companies; log every candidate / applied / skipped job in applications.json.
LinkedIn pacing: one search / results page at a time with a break of loop.linkedinSearchDelayMinutes in between, no bulk fetches. On HTTP 429 stop LinkedIn for the round and use company career sites.

autoApplyLoop._about: The step-by-step program Claude follows. The user clicks Search Google Jobs / Search LinkedIn on the job board; Claude searches in Chrome and adds about 10 candidates to the board (step 2g); the user approves jobs by putting them in the apply queue; Claude applies to queued jobs with queue runs started by the watcher (python jobboard.py watch).
autoApplyLoop.noNewPosts: If the queue is empty and no search button was clicked, the watcher does nothing.
steps: 1. Read job-search-config.json (all sections; the values of its ${...} placeholders come from ..\private\.env) and applications.json. Before analyzing ANY job, filter out jobs already logged (any status) with: python applog.py check "<company>" "<role>" [--id <job id>] - exit 0 = already logged, skip it (unless it is a Candidate / Needs approval job the user approved). Log every analyzed job with python applog.py add ...

1b. KEEP THE JOB LINK: every job logged in applications.json must have its link - always pass --url to python applog.py add: the company's own posting / application page for Submitted jobs, otherwise the LinkedIn post (https://www.linkedin.com/jobs/view/<id>/). applog.py refuses a Submitted entry without --url; python applog.py list --no-link shows entries still missing a link.

2. JOB SOURCES: candidates come from searches Claude runs in Chrome when the user clicks a search button on the job board (step 2g) - Google Jobs or LinkedIn, no SerpApi searches used. jobfeed.py (SerpApi Google Jobs, jobFeed section) is a manual tool only: run it only when the user asks; its jobs go on the board the same way.

2s. THE USER APPROVES THE JOBS: the job board page (http://127.0.0.1:<jobBoard.port>, opened by StartJobSearch.exe or `python jobboard.py`) lists the candidates; the user approves a job by putting it in the apply queue (in order) or skips it. Claude applies ONLY to queued jobs, with a QUEUE RUN (step 2q), started by the watcher (python jobboard.py watch, within seconds of an Add to apply queue click) or right away when the user says "apply my selected jobs". Never apply to, or log, jobs the user has not queued or has skipped.

2g. BROWSER SEARCH: the job board's "Search Google Jobs" / "Search LinkedIn" buttons save a search request; the watcher prints "search request <id>: google|linkedin". Then: (1) EVERY SEARCH COVERS ALL PREFERRED LOCATIONS: run the query once per entry in locations (each area, plus Remote US with the Remote filter) - never just one area. Pick the role searched least recently (`python jobboard.py searches --all` shows earlier requests and their notes) and run `python jobboard.py search <id> running --note "<query> in all locations"`. (1b) BUSIEST LOCATIONS FIRST: search the locations in the order of browserSearch.locationActivity (most entry-level openings first), and after the search update each location's counts there (date, entry-level results seen, candidates added) and re-sort so the busiest location is first. (2) Open a NEW Chrome tab (open_tab). Google Jobs: https://www.google.com/search?q=<query>+jobs+<area>&udm=8 (Google's Jobs tab), once per area, then the "Date posted" filter set to the last 24 hours (Past 24 hours / Yesterday). LinkedIn: the step 2b search URL sorted newest (sortBy=DD, f_TPR=r86400 = last 24 h per browserSearch.postedWithinHours, f_E=2,3, geoId / linkedinKeyword, f_WT=2 for Remote US), one results page, pace per loop.linkedinSearchDelayMinutes, stop on HTTP 429. (3) Read the results and open each promising post; keep up to browserSearch.candidatesPerSearch candidates that pass: title fits roles / seniority, experienceYears, skip.rules (active clearance, CBP, staffing agencies incl. jobFeed.staffingAgencies, LinkedIn Easy Apply only when the company's own posting cannot be found - look for it first per step 2c, skip companies, 2027-grad-only, Amazon SDE), salaryExpectation (drop jobs whose listed pay tops out below the expectation for their area; no salary listed = keep) and `python applog.py check` (already logged -> drop). LAST 24 HOURS ONLY, NO FILLING TO 10: look only at jobs posted in the last browserSearch.postedWithinHours (24) hours, newest first, in one pass over every location. candidatesPerSearch (10) is a cap, not a target: add whatever passes and stop - do NOT widen the time window, try related roles / synonyms, or go to career sites just to reach 10 (browserSearch.widenToFill = false). If nothing passes, say so in the search note. NO POST DATE: a posting that shows no posted date is NOT dropped for that - keep it as a candidate (and apply to it once queued) as long as it passes every other rule; note 'post date not given' in its description. For each, find the company's own posting / apply page ("Apply on company site", career site, ATS) as applyUrl. (4) Write them to a JSON file in the session scratchpad: [{source: "google"|"linkedin", id: <LinkedIn job id or a short unique id>, company, title, location, workMode: "Remote"|"Hybrid"|"On-site", salary (as posted, e.g. "$90,000 - $120,000" or "$40 - $55 /hr"), posted (ISO date-time), url (the post), applyUrl, description (COPY THE POSTING'S QUALIFICATIONS WORD FOR WORD, not a summary: 'Required: <every required / minimum / basic qualification line>' then 'Preferred: <every preferred / desired / nice-to-have line>', then a short summary of the role - the job board's keyword match score and years filter read only this text), companySize (employee range like "1,001-5,000", ONLY when a page already opened shows it, e.g. LinkedIn "1,001-5,000 employees" - never an extra lookup or search; omit if not shown)}] and run `python jobboard.py add <file> --search <id>` (marks the request done). Do NOT log them in applications.json - the user approves them on the board. (5) Close the search tab and list the candidates in chat: company, title, location, work mode, pay, years required, link - the user approves with Add to apply queue on the board, which starts a queue run (step 2q). (6) Blocked (CAPTCHA, sign-in, 429, no results): `python jobboard.py search <id> failed --note "<reason>"` and tell the user.

2u. UPDATE MY ANSWERS: the job board's "Update my answers" button lets the user upload a resume (saved in ..\private\uploads\) and then fill in a list of every application question (answerbank.py: the APPLICANT_* contact values, the ANSWER_* bank and common questions not in the bank yet; secrets are never shown). After an upload the watcher prints "profile request <id>: new resume <path>". Then: (1) `python jobboard.py profile running`. (2) Read the uploaded resume. (3) Update ..\private\resume.json to match it and make it the resume to upload (copy it to the resume path in step 4, or update that path, and ANSWER_RESUME_CURRENT_RESUME). (4) Fill every answer the resume gives - contact values, name, degree / school / graduation / GPA, current and previous job, total and per-skill years, skills, certifications, spoken languages - with `python answerbank.py set KEY "value"` (`python answerbank.py missing` lists the open questions); keep the user's existing answers unless the resume shows they changed. (5) `python jobboard.py profile done --note "<n> answers filled from the resume"` (or `failed --note <reason>`) - the page then shows the remaining questions to the user. Questions still blank are asked during applications and saved then (step 6d).

2q. QUEUE RUN: work through `python jobboard.py queue` top to bottom, one job at a time, in the browser named in launcher.browserTool (the browser-bridge tools in Google Chrome - in the job-only Chrome profile launcher.chromeProfileDir when it is set: its own job-site logins, none of the user's personal accounts). For each job: (1) `python jobboard.py applying <key>` (the page shows "Applying now"). (2) Open its apply link in a NEW tab (open_tab) - never reuse the tab of a blocked job. (3) Verify the posting per step 3; if it fails a rule, do not apply: log it as Needs approval with the reason, close the tab, next job. Jobs the queue lists as APPROVED BY THE USER (the board's Approve & apply button, applications.json status Approved) skip this check for the rule they failed - apply anyway. Jobs the queue lists as CONTINUE (the user clicked Continue application on a Needs User job - it goes back to the END of the queue) are finished where they stopped: reuse the tab left open if it is still there (else open the logged link), the user may have done the blocked step (sign-in, email code, CAPTCHA) - check the page and carry on. (4) Fill the application manually like a person - text fields, dropdowns, checkboxes, radio buttons, resume upload - with the ANSWER_* / APPLICANT_* values from ..\private\.env and the resume per steps 4 / 4a. (5) Account / sign-in pages per step 6b: sign in, or create the account, with APPLICANT_EMAIL + APPLICANT_PASSWORD (typed into the password fields only, never shown anywhere); if that password is empty or rejected, use the wait_for_password hand-off; then continue the same application. (6) The final Submit / Send / Apply button, per apply.autoSubmit: true -> click it, then `python applog.py add --status Submitted --id <job id> --url <link> ...` and close the tab; false -> fill every page up to that last button but do NOT click it: leave the tab open, `python applog.py add --status "Needs User" --id <job id> --url <link> --notes "READY TO SUBMIT: every field filled - review and click Submit in the open tab, then Mark as submitted on the board"`, and go on to the next job (a CONTINUE of such a job: if the page shows it was submitted, log Submitted; otherwise leave it for the user). (7) Blocked - password hand-off timed out, CAPTCHA, email verification code, site not allowed, a question the answer bank doesn't cover: leave that tab OPEN, `python applog.py add --status "Needs User" --id <job id> --url <link> --notes "<reason>; tab left open"` (it shows under "Waiting on you" on the board), then go straight to the next job in a new tab - never stop or wait on the whole queue for one blocked job. (8) Browser bridge errors: the bridge already retries each action 3 times; after that, re-read the page and try the step once more, then log the job as Needs User with the error and continue. If the extension is not connected at all, stop the queue run, tell the user once (check the extension badge) and leave the rest of the queue for the next run. End of the queue: a short summary - submitted, needs user (with the tabs left open), needs approval - and python applog.py note "queue run: <n> submitted, <n> needs user, <n> needs approval".
2a. FINISH THE QUEUE: a queue run handles EVERY job in `python jobboard.py queue` - each one Submitted, Needs approval, Needs User or Skipped with the reason in applications.json - before it ends.

2a2. CANDIDATE CAP + TIME LIMIT: once loop.candidateCapPerRound qualified candidates are found, stop searching and apply to those first. If finding candidates takes too long (more than ~30 minutes or 3 searches with nothing new), stop searching, apply to what was found, and wait for the next round. [superseded: no apply rounds any more - jobs are fetched by the job board, Claude applies only from the apply queue]

2b. LINKEDIN SEARCH: done through the board's Search LinkedIn button (step 2g) or when the user asks in chat - same steps. Search URL: LinkedIn job search (signed in), jobs posted in the last postedWithinHours hours (judge by the card text "Posted X minutes / hours ago"; use f_TPR=r86400 and read the card), experience level Entry level / Associate (f_E=2,3), ONE results page at a time with loop.linkedinSearchDelayMinutes between searches, areas = the locations list (linkedinGeoId / linkedinKeyword) plus Remote US (f_WT=2), roles = the roles list. On HTTP 429: stop. A queue run then opens the post, uses "Apply on company website" (never Easy Apply) and applies there.

2c. NO EASY APPLY: never apply through LinkedIn Easy Apply. FIND THE ORIGINAL POST: for every LinkedIn "Easy Apply" job, search for the same job on the company's own site before giving up - Google "<company> <exact job title> careers" (and "<company> <title> greenhouse OR lever OR ashby OR workday"), the company's careers page, and the ATS job APIs (Greenhouse / Lever / Ashby boards). Match on company + title + location (+ job id / requisition number if shown). Found -> use that page as applyUrl (step 2g) or apply there (step 2q) - never through Easy Apply. Not found -> candidate searches (2g): drop it; queue runs (2q): log it as Skipped with reason "Easy Apply - no company posting found" and list where you looked.

2c2. NO SIMPLIFY QUICK-APPLY: for SimplifyJobs jobs (board key simplify:...) never apply through Simplify's own Apply / quick-apply / Autopilot or a Simplify account. Open the company's own application page (the job's applyUrl, or the company careers / ATS link behind Simplify's APPLY NOW) and fill the form manually (step 4).

2d. COMPANY DAILY CAP: apply to the same company at most 2 times per calendar day. python applog.py check exits 2 when the cap is reached - then do not apply; log the job as Candidate with note "company daily cap".
3. Verify each candidate on the company's own posting against the seniority, experienceYears, skip and locations settings. A missing posted date is not a reason to skip.

3a. YEARS = GENERAL EXPERIENCE, NOT PER SKILL: compare a posting's years requirement with the user's general work experience, not their years in that specific skill ("2 years of <language>" counts as a 2-year requirement). Only experienceYears.stretchAt or more is skipped.

4. CLEAR match (up to experienceYears.max years, or new grad / level I, all rules pass) -> apply automatically using the ANSWER_* / APPLICANT_* entries in ..\private\.env and the resume ..\private\Resume.pdf. Log as Submitted with --url.

4a. EXPERIENCE FROM RESUME: fill every work-experience / education / skills section from ..\private\resume.json (structured copy of the resume PDF) - all jobs with title, company, location, from/to dates (MM/YYYY, "currently work here" for the current job), and always fill each "Role Description" / responsibilities box with that job's bullets (one per line, "- " prefix). If the resume PDF changes, update resume.json too.

4b. TAILORED RESUME PER JOB: `python jobboard.py queue` prints a `resume:` line for every job - UPLOAD THAT PDF for that job instead of the master resume. It is the master resume (resumeTailor.masterTex) with the keywords the user marked as 'I have this' on the job card added to the Technical Skills lines, built by the job board when the job was queued (tailor.py, pdfLaTeX). Also list those added keywords in the form's skills fields for that job. If the queue shows RESUME NOT READY, run `python tailor.py <key>` first; if it still fails, apply with the master resume and mention it in the log notes. Never edit the master .tex for one job. PLACE EACH ADDED KEYWORD: before uploading, for every keyword the queue lists under PLACE FIRST, decide from the master .tex and ..\private\resume.json whether the user's REAL experience already shows it. If one existing bullet truthfully covers it (e.g. the testing bullet for QA, firmware / device work for Embedded), reword ONLY that bullet to name the keyword - same facts, no new numbers, tools or claims, about the same length - with `python tailor.py place "<kw>" "<entry>" "<original LaTeX copied exactly>" "<new LaTeX>"`. If the experience does not show it, or saying so would no longer be true, keep it on the Technical Skills line only: `python tailor.py place "<kw>" skills`. Placements are saved (keyword-placements.json) and reused for later jobs; placing rebuilds the queued resume. Mention each reworded bullet in the queue run summary.
5. STRETCH / unclear (experienceYears.stretchAt years, unusual tech, low pay) -> log as "Needs approval" in applications.json, do not apply.

6. BLOCKED (sign-in, new account, password, CAPTCHA, arbitration agreement, unknown personal question) -> fill what is possible, LEAVE THE TAB OPEN, log as "Needs User" with the tab / URL; the user finishes manually. FILE PICKERS ARE NOT A BLOCK: when a resume / file field has no <input type=file> (only a 'Choose File' / 'Upload' button or a drop zone, e.g. Apple Jobs), call the browser-bridge upload_file with the BUTTON's ref - the bridge intercepts the file chooser the click opens and fills it (no OS dialog). Only if that reports 'opened no file chooser' log Needs User.

6b. LOGIN PAGES / NEW ACCOUNTS: use ${APPLICANT_EMAIL} and the password in ${APPLICANT_PASSWORD} (..\private\.env) to sign in, or to CREATE an account when the site has none for that email (Create account / Register: email, password + confirm, name, privacy/accept checkboxes). Type the password straight into the password fields only - never print it in chat, logs, notes, applications.json or any other file. Retry each step up to 3 times. If APPLICANT_PASSWORD is empty, or the site rejects it (password rules, existing account with another password), fall back to the wait_for_password hand-off (the user fills it with Chrome's password manager). Email verification codes / CAPTCHAs still need the user: leave the tab open, log it as Needs User, and continue with the next job. List all waiting tabs in the queue run summary. When sign-in fails (account unverified, password rejected, sign-in does nothing), always try Create Account next with the same email and password before resending a verification email; only if account creation is refused fall back to Forgot password / verification email and log Needs User. TYPE_SECRET: type the password with the browser bridge tool type_secret (name APPLICANT_PASSWORD, ref = the password field) - the bridge reads it from private/.env and types it, Claude never reads or sees the value (reading it via Bash is blocked by the permission check). Use it for every password + confirm field; wait_for_password only if type_secret fails or the site rejects the password.

6c. SITE NOT ALLOWED: if the browser bridge says "Site not allowed: <domain>", do not stop or wait - log the job as "Needs User" with note "site not allowed: <domain>" + the URL, leave the tab open, and continue with the next job. Mention blocked domains in the queue run summary.

6d. SAVE EVERY NEW ANSWER: when a form asks a question the ANSWER_* bank does not cover and the user answers it, immediately run: python applog.py answer --section <matching '# --- section ---' in ..\private\.env> --question "<the question>" --answer "<the answer>" - it adds / updates the entry in ..\private\.env (and the empty key in ..\examples\.env.example). Reuse that answer on later forms without asking again.

6e. VERIFICATION EMAILS / CODES ARE NOT A BLOCK: when a site sends a verification email ("verify your account", Workday after Create Account, Greenhouse / Oracle email codes), note the time, start `python mailcheck.py wait --match <company>,<site e.g. myworkday / greenhouse / oracle> --since <that time> --every 120 --timeout 1200` IN THE BACKGROUND (Bash run_in_background - it checks the job-application inbox every 2 minutes, read-only) and go on with the next queued job meanwhile. When it reports {link} open the link in the job's tab (verifies the account), sign in and continue the application; when it reports {code} type the code into the waiting field and continue. Only when it times out (20 min) or mailcheck is not set up (MAIL_CLIENT_ID empty / not signed in: python mailcheck.py login) log Needs User as before. Never use it for anything but the current application's verification mail.

7. Never print, log or copy the account password anywhere (it lives only in ..\private\.env as APPLICANT_PASSWORD and is typed only into a site's password fields), never solve CAPTCHAs. Close tabs of finished/skipped jobs.
8. End each queue run with a short summary of submitted / needs approval / needs user (with the tabs left open).

answersSource: The application answer bank lives in ..\private\.env as ANSWER_* keys (plus APPLICANT_* for contact). Read it before every application; save each newly answered question with: python applog.py answer --section S --question Q --answer A (autoApplyLoop step 6d).

matchScore._about: Keyword match score on each job board card (JobSearch/matchscore.py): plain rules, no AI / no tokens. Score = matched / found: how many of the tech keywords in the post (title + required + desired / preferred qualifications) are on your resume.json - more matches, higher score; shown as e.g. '78% · 7/9'. Experience, level, location and pay are NOT part of it (judge those yourself on the card). Labels: Strong 80+, Good 65+, Fair 50+, Low below; 'no keywords' = the post's text names no known terms. `python matchscore.py` lists every board job's score; `--profile` shows the keywords read from your resume; add terms to VOCAB in matchscore.py.

resumeTailor._about: Tailored resume per job (JobSearch/tailor.py): keywords the user clicks as 'I have this' on a job card are added to the matching Technical Skills line of a copy of masterTex (in private/), compiled with pdfLaTeX (MiKTeX) to private/<outDir>/<job>/<pdfName> when the job is in the apply queue; the queue run uploads that PDF. masterPdf = the resume used for jobs without added keywords. maxPages = warn when the PDF gets longer.
